sections.title: Introduction to English
sections.content:
Why Learn English?

English is the global language of business, science, and international communication. Mastering English opens doors to countless opportunities in career advancement and personal development.

Key Benefits

  • Career Advancement - Many multinational companies require English proficiency
  • Access to Information - Most academic resources are in English
  • Global Communication - Connect with people worldwide
  • Cultural Understanding - Appreciate literature, films, and music in their original form

sections.title: English Tenses
sections.content:
Understanding Tenses

Tenses indicate the time of an action or state of being. English has 12 main tenses divided into three time frames: past, present, and future.

Present Tenses

  • Simple Present - I work every day.
  • Present Continuous - I am working now.
  • Present Perfect - I have worked here for five years.
  • Present Perfect Continuous - I have been working since morning.

Past Tenses

  • Simple Past - I worked yesterday.
  • Past Continuous - I was working when you called.
  • Past Perfect - I had worked before the meeting.
  • Past Perfect Continuous - I had been working for hours.

Future Tenses

  • Simple Future - I will work tomorrow.
  • Future Continuous - I will be working at 9 AM.
  • Future Perfect - I will have worked by then.
  • Future Perfect Continuous - I will have been working for a year.

sections.title: Professional Vocabulary
sections.content:
Business English Vocabulary

Common Office Terms

WordMeaningExample
DeadlineBatas waktuThe deadline is next Friday.
MeetingRapatWe have a meeting at 10 AM.
ReportLaporanPlease submit your report.
ProposalUsulanI will prepare the proposal.
BudgetAnggaranThe budget is limited.
ScheduleJadwalCheck the schedule first.

Useful Phrases

  • "I would like to..." - Saya ingin...
  • "Could you please..." - Bisakah Anda...
  • "I appreciate your help." - Saya menghargai bantuan Anda.
  • "Let me get back to you." - Saya akan menghubungi Anda kembali.

sections.title: Business Writing
sections.content:
Professional Email Writing

Email Structure

  • Subject Line - Clear and concise topic
  • Greeting - Dear Mr./Ms. [Name]
  • Opening - State your purpose
  • Body - Provide details
  • Closing - Summarize and call to action
  • Sign-off - Best regards, Sincerely

Sample Email

Subject: Meeting Request - Project Update

Dear Mr. Johnson,

I hope this email finds you well. I am writing to request a meeting to discuss the progress of our current project.

Would you be available next Tuesday at 2 PM? Please let me know if this time works for you.

Best regards,
Ahmad

sections.title: Speaking Skills
sections.content:
Improving Speaking Skills

Presentation Tips

  1. Prepare - Know your material thoroughly
  2. Practice - Rehearse multiple times
  3. Speak Clearly - Enunciate and pace yourself
  4. Engage - Make eye contact with your audience
  5. Use Visual Aids - Support your points with slides

Common Phrases for Presentations

  • "Good morning/afternoon, everyone."
  • "Today, I will be presenting..."
  • "Let me begin by..."
  • "Moving on to the next point..."
  • "To summarize..."
  • "Thank you for your attention."
  • "Are there any questions?"
